questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: The things a person or a society considers important, good and worth keeping are called
questions.explanation: Values are the beliefs and things people regard as important and desirable, which guide how they behave.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: Which of the following is an attribute of an honest person?
options: Hiding the truth to avoid blame
Keeping promises and telling the truth
questions.explanation: An honest person is truthful, keeps promises and does not deceive others.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: Emeka sold his old phone to a classmate and told him that the battery was weak before collecting payment. Emeka's action shows
questions.explanation: Telling a buyer the truth about the faults in what is being sold, even when it may reduce the price, is honesty.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: Which of the following is a benefit of honesty to a nation?
options: It builds trust between government and citizens
It increases the number of court cases
It encourages people to hide wrongdoing
questions.explanation: When leaders and citizens are honest, people trust one another and the government, and this helps development.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: A certificate obtained through examination malpractice is likely to harm the holder in the long run mainly because the holder
options: lacks the knowledge and skills the certificate claims
will be given too many jobs
will be praised for hard work
will no longer need to read
questions.explanation: Cheating gives a paper qualification without the real knowledge behind it, so the person fails when asked to perform and may also be exposed and punished.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: Sharing, caring and supporting one another are attributes of
questions.explanation: Cooperation means working together, and its attributes include sharing, caring and supporting others.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: Members of a market association contribute money every month to repair the roof of their market. This is an example of
questions.explanation: People coming together and pooling resources to achieve a common goal is cooperation.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely to WEAKEN cooperation in a group?
options: Distrust and unfair sharing of benefits
questions.explanation: Cooperation grows with trust, fairness and communication; distrust and unfair sharing make members unwilling to work together.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: A group project was completed early because each member did a part of the work and helped others. This shows that one benefit of cooperation is
questions.explanation: When people cooperate, work is shared and supported, so the group achieves its goals faster and better.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: A self-reliant person is one who
options: waits for others to provide everything
depends mainly on his or her own effort and skills
questions.explanation: Self-reliance is the ability to depend on one's own abilities, talents and efforts to meet one's needs.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: The correct order of developing a talent is
options: identifying it, nurturing it and perfecting it
perfecting it, identifying it and nurturing it
nurturing it, perfecting it and identifying it
hiding it, identifying it and selling it
questions.explanation: A talent must first be discovered (identified), then trained and encouraged (nurtured), and then improved through practice (perfected).

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: Which of the following is a benefit of self-reliance to the family?
options: It reduces the burden on parents and relatives
questions.explanation: When members can provide for themselves, the family is less burdened and can even be supported by them.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: A country that has rich natural resources but whose youths lack skills will most likely
options: become the richest country in the world quickly
depend on other countries for skilled work and finished goods
questions.explanation: Natural resources need skilled human resources to turn them into wealth; without skills, the country imports expertise and products.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem: The factors that promote a good value system in a society include
questions.explanation: Consistency, trust, tolerance, fairness, integrity and commitment help values to be held firmly in a society.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: Fair-play and truthfulness are attributes of
questions.explanation: Integrity involves probity, honesty, truthfulness, fair-play and refusal to compromise good principles.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: Why does a society need people of integrity in public offices?
options: So that public servants can become rich quickly
So that rules can be ignored
So that only friends are employed
So that public funds and trust are not abused
questions.explanation: People of integrity do not steal, take bribes or bend rules, so public money is protected and citizens can trust leaders.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: A judge refused to change her judgement even after she was threatened and offered money. This shows that she does not
questions.explanation: Non-compromise of principles is an attribute of integrity: the judge stood by what was right despite pressure.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: Contentment means
options: being satisfied with what one has
questions.explanation: A contented person is satisfied with what he or she has legitimately earned and does not envy others.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: Which of the following social problems is MOST closely linked to lack of contentment?
questions.explanation: People who are not contented may turn to greed, corruption, cheating and robbery to get what they want.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: Humility and rejection of greed are attributes of
questions.explanation: A contented person is humble, lacks envy and rejects greed and corruption.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: Self-control, moderation and respect for rules are attributes of
questions.explanation: Discipline is the ability to control oneself and behave according to rules and accepted standards.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: Ada wanted to watch a film, but she first finished her assignment because she had a test the next day. Ada showed
questions.explanation: Putting duties before pleasure and controlling one's desires is self-discipline.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: A student who continues to train for a race after failing to win three times is showing which attribute of discipline?
questions.explanation: Perseverance means continuing steadily towards a goal in spite of difficulties or failure.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: The three types of courage are
questions.explanation: Courage is commonly grouped into physical courage, moral courage and spiritual courage.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: A man jumped into a burning building to rescue a trapped child. This act shows
questions.explanation: Facing physical danger or pain to do something good is physical courage.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem: Which of these is an example of spiritual courage?
options: Holding firmly to one's faith and hope during a long illness
questions.explanation: Spiritual courage is inner strength drawn from faith and conviction that helps a person stay firm in hardship.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: A worker who produces the same good quality of work every day, and not only when the supervisor is watching, is showing
questions.explanation: Consistency means maintaining the same high standard of work and behaviour at all times.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: A worker who works hard, carefully and steadily is said to be
questions.explanation: Diligence is careful and persistent effort in one's work.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: A civil servant who keeps clear records and allows his work to be checked by others is showing
questions.explanation: Transparency means being open in one's dealings so that one's work can be checked and trusted.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason for rewarding workers who perform well?
options: It reduces the quality of work
It motivates them and others to be more productive
questions.explanation: Rewards such as promotion, awards and recognition motivate workers, raising productivity and efficiency.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: Going to work every working day without unnecessary absence shows
questions.explanation: Regularity means being present consistently at work and performing duties without unnecessary absence.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: An aircraft engineer skips safety checks on a plane to finish work early. The most likely consequence of this attitude is
options: an air disaster that may cost lives
questions.explanation: Wrong attitude to work in sensitive jobs can lead to national disasters on air, sea or road, and loss of lives.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: When many workers in a country lack the right attitude to work, the country's image abroad is likely to
questions.explanation: Poor productivity, corruption and failure of services damage how other countries see a nation, while good work culture improves national image.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: Which of these shows the RIGHT attitude to work?
options: Doing one's duties well even when the supervisor is absent
Leaving the office before closing time
Using office time for private business
questions.explanation: A worker with the right attitude is committed and honest, doing the job well whether or not anyone is watching.

questions.topic: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
questions.stem: Lack of motivation among workers usually leads to
questions.explanation: Workers who are not motivated put in less effort, so productivity falls.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a negative behaviour?
questions.explanation: Disregard for time, such as habitual lateness, is listed among negative behaviours.

questions.stem: Membership of secret, violent groups in schools is known as
questions.explanation: Cultism is membership of secret and often violent groups, and it is a negative behaviour.

questions.stem: A person who loves money so much that he does anything, legal or illegal, to get it is showing
questions.explanation: Excessive love of money leads people to fraud, corruption and other crimes.

questions.stem: Value disorientation means
options: the teaching of values in schools
a situation where people no longer follow good societal values
questions.explanation: Value disorientation occurs when society loses or abandons its good values and begins to accept wrong behaviour.

questions.stem: Which of these is a likely effect of cultism in a school?
options: Fear, violence and disruption of academic activities
questions.explanation: Cult groups use secrecy and violence, which creates fear, injuries and disruption of learning.

questions.stem: Why does negative behaviour lead to inefficiency in public offices?
options: Officers who are corrupt or lazy do not perform their duties properly
It increases the number of skilled workers
questions.explanation: When workers are dishonest, lazy or careless with time, jobs are done badly or not at all, making the system inefficient.

questions.stem: Which of the following can help to promote positive behaviour among students?
questions.explanation: Rewarding good conduct encourages students to keep behaving well and others to copy them.

questions.stem: Parents can help to discourage negative behaviour in their children mainly by
options: giving them money without asking how it is spent
allowing them to keep bad company
being good role models and correcting them
questions.explanation: Children learn from what they see; parents who model good values and correct bad behaviour help to build positive behaviour.

questions.stem: Which of these is the BEST reason why drug trafficking is regarded as a negative behaviour?
options: It destroys lives and promotes crime
It is approved by the law
questions.explanation: Drug trafficking is illegal and harmful: it destroys the health of users and fuels other crimes.

questions.stem: Examination malpractice is a negative behaviour because it
options: rewards cheating instead of hard work
questions.explanation: Examination malpractice is dishonest; it rewards cheating and lowers the value of certificates.

questions.stem: A person who is a legal member of a country and enjoys its rights is called a
questions.explanation: A citizen is a legally recognised member of a state who enjoys its rights and performs duties to it.

questions.stem: The three ways of becoming a Nigerian citizen are by
questions.explanation: The Nigerian constitution provides for citizenship by birth, by registration and by naturalisation.

questions.stem: A person born outside Nigeria whose grandparent is a Nigerian citizen may become a citizen by
questions.explanation: The constitution allows a person born outside Nigeria to a grandparent who is a citizen to become a citizen by registration.

questions.stem: Citizenship by naturalisation is granted mainly to
options: foreigners who have lived in Nigeria for a long period and meet the conditions
questions.explanation: Naturalisation is for foreigners who satisfy conditions such as long residence, good character and willingness to swear allegiance.

questions.stem: Before a foreigner is granted Nigerian citizenship by naturalisation, he or she must
options: take an oath of allegiance to Nigeria
questions.explanation: Taking the oath of allegiance is a requirement, showing loyalty to Nigeria.

questions.stem: The main difference between citizenship by birth and citizenship by naturalisation is that citizenship by birth
options: must be applied for, while naturalisation is automatic
can only be given by a traditional ruler
comes automatically from one's parents or grandparents, while naturalisation is applied for
questions.explanation: A person is a citizen by birth through Nigerian parentage or ancestry; naturalisation must be applied for and approved.

questions.stem: A person who lives in a country but is not its citizen is called
questions.explanation: An alien is a foreigner living in a country of which he or she is not a citizen.

questions.stem: Which of these is a privilege usually enjoyed by citizens but NOT by aliens in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Voting and being voted for are political rights reserved for citizens.

questions.stem: Which of these is a usual requirement for citizenship by naturalisation in Nigeria?
options: Being of good character and able to contribute to the country
Owning a house in every state
questions.explanation: Applicants must be of good character, have lived in Nigeria for the required period and be able to contribute to its progress.

questions.stem: Good citizenship is shown when a person
options: obeys the laws of the country
questions.explanation: A good citizen obeys the law, pays taxes and contributes to national development.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: The things a citizen is expected to do for the country are called
questions.explanation: Duties are obligations that citizens owe to the state, such as obeying laws and paying taxes.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: A citizen who is arrested has the right to be brought before a court within a reasonable time. This protects the right to
questions.explanation: The right to personal liberty protects people from unlawful or indefinite detention; arrested persons must be charged to court within a reasonable time.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: Paying tax is a duty of a citizen because
options: it is a form of punishment
it provides money for government to provide services
it gives citizens power to break laws
questions.explanation: Taxes provide the revenue government needs to build schools, hospitals and roads for everyone.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: The fundamental human rights of Nigerians are contained in which chapter of the 1999 constitution?
questions.explanation: Chapter IV of the 1999 constitution (as amended) contains the fundamental rights.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: Which of these is a right and not a duty?
questions.explanation: Freedom of movement is a right citizens enjoy; the others are duties citizens owe.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: Rights and duties help to maintain social control in a society because
options: rights allow people to do anything they like
duties are only for government workers
they encourage people to ignore the law
when people know what they can do and what they must do, conflict is reduced
questions.explanation: Rights and duties set limits on behaviour so people respect one another, which brings order, peace and discipline.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: A person's rights can be limited by law when
options: exercising them threatens public safety or the rights of others
the person belongs to a different religion
questions.explanation: Rights are not absolute; they can be lawfully restricted in the interest of public safety, order, health or others' rights.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: Which of the following is a duty of a citizen?
options: Defending the country when called upon
questions.explanation: Defending the nation is a duty; the other options are rights.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: The right of an accused person to be told the charge against him and to defend himself in court is the right to
questions.explanation: Fair hearing means being informed of the charge, given time to prepare and allowed to defend oneself before an impartial court.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: Due process means that
options: leaders can punish anyone they dislike
people are dealt with according to laid-down legal procedures
questions.explanation: Due process means following the proper legal procedure before anyone is punished or deprived of a right.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem: Joining a club or a lawful association of one's choice is an example of the right to
questions.explanation: Freedom of association allows people to form or belong to lawful groups, unions and parties.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, the highest law of the land is the
questions.explanation: The constitution is the supreme law; all other laws must agree with it.

questions.stem: Supremacy of the constitution means that
options: every person and authority, including government, must obey the constitution
the President is above the constitution
the constitution can be ignored in emergencies
only judges must obey the constitution
questions.explanation: Under the supremacy of the constitution, all persons and authorities are bound by it and no one is above it.

questions.stem: A government action that goes against the constitution is said to be
questions.explanation: Any action or law that is against the constitution is unconstitutional and can be set aside by the courts.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST shows the supremacy of the constitution in Nigeria?
options: A council chairman opens a market
A court cancels a state law that conflicts with the constitution
questions.explanation: When courts strike down laws that conflict with the constitution, it shows the constitution is above all other laws.

questions.stem: Who is bound to obey the provisions of the Nigerian constitution?
options: All persons and authorities in Nigeria
questions.explanation: The constitution binds everyone in Nigeria, citizens and government alike.

questions.stem: Why is it important that the constitution should be supreme?
options: It prevents leaders from ruling arbitrarily
It allows leaders to change laws at will
It removes the need for elections
questions.explanation: A supreme constitution limits the powers of leaders and protects citizens from arbitrary rule.

questions.stem: A constitution that is written down in one document is called a
questions.explanation: A written constitution is contained in a single document, like Nigeria's constitution.

questions.stem: A constitution that can be amended only through a difficult and special procedure is described as
questions.explanation: A rigid constitution needs a special procedure to change it, such as approval by a large majority of the legislature and states.

questions.stem: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 is named after
options: Sir Hugh Clifford, a colonial Governor
questions.explanation: The 1922 constitution was introduced by Sir Hugh Clifford, then Governor of Nigeria.

questions.stem: The first political party in Nigeria, formed after the elective principle was introduced in 1922, was the
options: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons
questions.explanation: Herbert Macaulay formed the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP) in 1923 to contest the elective seats.

questions.stem: One major criticism of the Richards Constitution of 1946 was that
options: Nigerians were not consulted before it was made
questions.explanation: Nationalists criticised the Richards Constitution because Nigerians were not consulted in drawing it up.

questions.stem: The constitution that was made after wide consultation with Nigerians at village, provincial and regional levels was the
questions.explanation: Before the Macpherson Constitution, Nigerians were consulted at many levels, ending in a General Conference at Ibadan in 1950.

questions.stem: Under the Lyttelton Constitution of 1954, Lagos was
options: made the capital of the Northern Region
questions.explanation: The 1954 Lyttelton Constitution created a federation and separated Lagos as a federal territory.

questions.stem: Under the Independence Constitution of 1960, the British monarch was represented in Nigeria by the
questions.explanation: Nigeria remained in the Commonwealth with the British monarch as Head of State, represented by a Governor-General.

questions.stem: The 1963 Republican Constitution made the Supreme Court of Nigeria the final court of appeal instead of the
questions.explanation: Before 1963, final appeals went to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London; the Republican Constitution ended this.

questions.stem: Which of these was a feature of the 1979 Constitution?
options: Separation of powers between an executive president and the National Assembly
A Prime Minister as head of government
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution introduced the presidential system with an executive president and a separate National Assembly.

questions.stem: The 1989 Constitution of Nigeria is remembered as a constitution that
options: was not fully put into operation
questions.explanation: The 1989 Constitution was meant for a Third Republic but was never fully implemented before military rule continued.

questions.stem: Nigeria became independent from Britain on
questions.explanation: Nigeria gained independence on 1st October 1960 under the Independence Constitution.

questions.stem: The constitution under which Nigeria has been governed since the return to civilian rule in 1999 is the
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended, is the constitution in force.

questions.stem: A constitution performs which of the following functions?
options: It defines the powers of government and the rights of citizens
It decides the prices of goods
questions.explanation: A constitution sets out how a country is governed, the powers of each organ of government and the rights of citizens.

questions.stem: Which of these is a national symbol of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: National symbols such as the coat of arms, national flag, anthem, pledge and currency represent the whole country.

questions.stem: The Nigerian national currency is the
questions.explanation: Nigeria's currency is the naira, divided into 100 kobo; it replaced the Nigerian pound in 1973.

questions.stem: The two horses on the Nigerian coat of arms represent
questions.explanation: The two white horses (chargers) on the coat of arms stand for dignity.

questions.stem: The black shield on the Nigerian coat of arms represents
questions.explanation: The black shield stands for Nigeria's fertile soil.

questions.stem: The Nigerian national flag was designed by
questions.explanation: The green-white-green flag was designed by Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi, a Nigerian student, in 1959.

questions.stem: The white colour in the Nigerian national flag stands for
questions.explanation: Green stands for agriculture and natural wealth, while white stands for peace and unity.

questions.stem: Saying the National Pledge shows a citizen's
questions.explanation: The pledge is a promise of loyalty, honesty and service to Nigeria.

questions.stem: The National Pledge begins with the words
questions.explanation: The National Pledge begins "I pledge to Nigeria my country, to be faithful, loyal and honest".

questions.stem: The yellow flowers at the base of the Nigerian coat of arms are
questions.explanation: Costus spectabilis, Nigeria's national flower, appears at the base of the coat of arms.

questions.stem: The Federal Character principle helps national unity mainly by
options: giving all jobs to one region
giving every state and group a fair share of federal appointments
questions.explanation: Federal Character ensures appointments and opportunities are spread across states and groups so none feels left out.

questions.stem: Corps members in the NYSC are usually posted to states other than their own so that they can
options: learn about other cultures and promote unity
questions.explanation: Serving outside one's state exposes graduates to other cultures and builds understanding and national unity.

questions.stem: Which of the following attitudes would MOST promote national unity among Nigerians of different ethnic groups?
options: Hiring only people from one's town
questions.explanation: Treating people fairly regardless of ethnic group and tolerating differences helps Nigerians live together in unity.

questions.stem: Hospitality as a way of promoting national unity means
questions.explanation: Hospitality is kindness to guests and strangers, which helps people from different places feel at home.

questions.stem: Nigeria adopted the federal system of government formally in
questions.explanation: The Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 formally made Nigeria a federation.

questions.stem: The component units that make up the Nigerian federation, apart from the Federal Capital Territory, are called
questions.explanation: The federating units of Nigeria today are the 36 states, together with the Federal Capital Territory.

questions.stem: Countries with many ethnic groups often adopt federalism because it
options: gives all power to one person
questions.explanation: Federalism lets different groups manage some local affairs while remaining united under one country.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries, like Nigeria, operates a federal system of government?
questions.explanation: The USA is a federation of states; the United Kingdom, Ghana and France are unitary states.

questions.stem: Which of these is a feature of a federation but NOT of a unitary state?
options: There is a head of state
Laws are made by a legislature
Component units have powers that the central government cannot take away by ordinary law
questions.explanation: In a federation the constitution guarantees the powers of the states; in a unitary state the centre can take back delegated powers.

questions.stem: The capital of Nigeria moved from Lagos to Abuja officially in
questions.explanation: The Federal Capital was officially moved from Lagos to Abuja in December 1991.

questions.stem: In a federation, disputes between the federal government and a state government are settled by the
questions.explanation: The courts, especially the Supreme Court, interpret the constitution and settle disputes between tiers of government.

questions.stem: Another name for the central government in a federation is the
questions.explanation: The central government of a federation is called the federal government.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a demerit of federalism in Nigeria?
options: It gives no room for local control
It is expensive to run many governments
questions.explanation: Running federal, state and local governments with their officials and legislatures is costly.

questions.stem: Federalism helps to control the activities of states in Nigeria mainly because
options: states have armies of their own
the constitution sets limits to what each state can do
questions.explanation: Under federalism, the constitution defines the powers of states, and important matters like defence and currency remain federal.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: Which tier of government is closest to the people at the grassroots?
questions.explanation: Local government operates at the grassroots, closest to the people.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: Nigeria has how many local government areas recognised by the constitution?
questions.explanation: The constitution lists 774 local government areas in Nigeria.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: Which of these matters is on the Exclusive Legislative List?
questions.explanation: Defence is reserved for the federal government on the Exclusive Legislative List.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: The law-making body of a state is the
questions.explanation: Each state has a House of Assembly that makes laws for the state.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: The head of the executive arm of a state government is the
questions.explanation: The Governor heads the executive arm of a state.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: If a valid federal law and a state law on a concurrent matter conflict, then
options: the federal law prevails and the state law is void to the extent of the conflict
questions.explanation: On concurrent matters, where federal and state laws conflict, the federal law prevails.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: Laws made by a local government council are called
questions.explanation: Local government councils make bye-laws for their areas.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: Which of these BEST describes the relationship between the tiers of government in Nigeria?
options: The local government controls the federal government
Each tier can do whatever it likes
The state government appoints the President
Each tier performs functions according to the constitution and cooperates with the others
questions.explanation: The tiers are coordinate and interdependent: each carries out constitutional functions and they work together.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: Which of these is a function of the federal government?
questions.explanation: Currency is an exclusive federal matter, handled by the Central Bank of Nigeria.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem: The executive head of a local government council in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: Each local government council is headed by an elected Chairman.

questions.stem: A body of rules made by government that every member of society must obey is called
questions.explanation: Laws are rules made by government and enforced by state institutions.

questions.stem: The scholar best known for explaining the principles of the rule of law is
questions.explanation: A. V. Dicey, a British jurist, explained the rule of law in terms of supremacy of the law, equality before the law and protection of rights.

questions.stem: Equality before the law means that
options: leaders cannot be charged to court for anything
only citizens can go to court
the same law applies to everyone, rich or poor
questions.explanation: Equality before the law means no one is above the law and everyone is treated equally by it.

questions.stem: Which of these is a benefit of the rule of law over arbitrary rule?
questions.explanation: Under the rule of law, citizens' rights are protected and government acts only according to law.

questions.stem: A principle of the rule of law states that no one should be punished except
options: for a breach of law proved before a court
questions.explanation: A person can be punished only for breaking an existing law and only after a fair trial.

questions.stem: Which of these situations violates the rule of law?
options: A court acquits an innocent person
A thief is tried and sentenced by a court
A governor orders that a critic be detained without trial
questions.explanation: Detaining a person without trial on a leader's orders is arbitrary and violates the rule of law.

questions.stem: Payment of money ordered by a court as punishment for an offence is called a
questions.explanation: A fine is a sum of money a court orders an offender to pay as punishment.

questions.stem: Which of these is a limitation to the rule of law in Nigeria?
options: Immunity enjoyed by some public officers while in office
questions.explanation: Constitutional immunity from civil and criminal proceedings for some officers while in office limits equality before the law.

questions.stem: Which arm of government interprets the law and decides cases?
questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets laws and settles disputes through the courts.

questions.stem: Service to the community ordered by a court instead of imprisonment, such as sweeping public places, is called
questions.explanation: Community service is a punishment in which a court orders an offender to do unpaid work for the public.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: Which of these is a civil society organisation that works to protect human rights in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Civil Liberties Organisation (CLO) is a non-governmental group that defends human rights in Nigeria.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: The Committee for the Defence of Human Rights (CDHR) mainly
options: speaks out and takes action against human rights abuses
questions.explanation: CDHR is a civil society group that exposes and challenges human rights violations.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: Media coverage helps to protect human rights mainly by
options: exposing violations to the public and authorities
questions.explanation: When the media report abuses, public pressure forces authorities to act and deters violators.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) protects the rights of
questions.explanation: Trade unions such as the NLC protect workers' rights, wages and working conditions.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: A poor woman whose house was illegally demolished wants to go to court but cannot afford a lawyer. The BEST body for her to approach is the
questions.explanation: The Legal Aid Council provides free legal services to people who cannot afford lawyers.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: A refusal to eat as a way of drawing attention to injustice is called a
questions.explanation: A hunger strike is a peaceful protest in which people refuse food to draw attention to an injustice.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: Why is it important that protest marches to defend human rights remain peaceful?
options: Violence can lead to loss of lives and violates the rights of others
Violence makes the courts support the protesters
questions.explanation: Violent protests endanger lives and property and abuse the rights of others; peaceful protest is a legitimate way to demand rights.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) is an example of a
options: students' union that can speak up for students' rights
questions.explanation: Students' unions such as NANS speak up for students' rights and welfare.

questions.topic: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
questions.stem: Which government body was set up in Nigeria to promote and protect human rights and receive complaints of abuse?
questions.explanation: The National Human Rights Commission investigates complaints of rights abuses and promotes respect for human rights.

questions.stem: The consumer right to satisfaction of basic needs means that people should have access to
options: essential goods and services such as food, water, shelter and health care
questions.explanation: Satisfaction of basic needs refers to access to essential goods and services needed for survival and decent living.

questions.stem: The right of a consumer to be protected from goods that are dangerous to health or life is the right to
questions.explanation: The right to safety protects consumers against hazardous goods and services.

questions.stem: The right to be heard (representation) means that consumers' views should be
options: considered when policies on goods and services are made
questions.explanation: Consumers have a right to have their interests represented when government and businesses make decisions affecting them.

questions.stem: Keeping the receipt after buying a product is important because it
options: serves as proof of the transaction if there is a complaint
reduces the price of the product
questions.explanation: Receipts, invoices and warranties are proofs that a consumer needs to seek redress.

questions.stem: The Nigerian government agency that protects consumers against unfair business practices is the
options: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC)
questions.explanation: The FCCPC protects consumers and promotes fair competition in Nigeria.

questions.stem: A consumer who checks the NAFDAC registration number and expiry date before buying canned food is exercising which responsibility?
questions.explanation: Responsible consumers are aware and alert about the quality and safety of what they buy.

questions.stem: A consumer who reports a fake product to the authorities instead of keeping quiet is fulfilling the responsibility to
questions.explanation: Speaking out about bad products and unfair practices protects other consumers and is a consumer responsibility.

questions.stem: Consumers have a responsibility to respect the environment. Which of these actions fulfils this?
options: Disposing of empty bottles and wrappers properly
questions.explanation: Respecting the environment means disposing of waste properly so that the environment remains healthy for all.

questions.stem: Consumer education helps consumers to
options: make wise choices when buying goods and services
questions.explanation: Consumer education gives people knowledge and skills to choose and buy wisely and to know their rights.

questions.stem: Thinking independently as a consumer means
options: not buying a product just because of advertisements or pressure from others
questions.explanation: An independent consumer judges products on their own merit rather than being swayed by adverts or peer pressure.

questions.stem: The word democracy comes from two Greek words, "demos" and "kratos", which mean
questions.explanation: "Demos" means people and "kratos" means rule or power, so democracy means rule by the people.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a pressure group in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Professional bodies such as the Nigeria Medical Association try to influence government policy without seeking to rule, so they are pressure groups.

questions.stem: The two chambers of the Nigerian National Assembly are the
options: Senate and the House of Representatives
Senate and the State House of Assembly
House of Chiefs and House of Representatives
questions.explanation: The National Assembly is bicameral: the Senate and the House of Representatives.

questions.stem: Which of these is a feature of democracy?
questions.explanation: In a democracy, elections are held regularly so people can choose or change their leaders.

questions.stem: A main function of political parties in a democracy is to
questions.explanation: Political parties sponsor candidates, present programmes and seek to win power through elections.

questions.stem: Pressure groups differ from political parties because pressure groups
options: seek to influence government without contesting elections to take power
questions.explanation: Pressure groups try to influence policies; political parties seek to win elections and control government.

questions.stem: Which of these is an importance of democracy?
options: It allows leaders to stay in power forever
It removes the rights of minorities
It gives citizens a say in how they are governed
questions.explanation: Democracy allows citizens to participate in decision-making through voting and expression of opinion.

questions.stem: The type of democracy in which citizens elect people to make decisions on their behalf is
questions.explanation: In representative democracy, people elect representatives who govern on their behalf, as in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Why is direct democracy difficult to practise in a large country like Nigeria?
options: The population is too large for everyone to meet and decide on every issue
questions.explanation: Direct democracy requires every citizen to take part in decisions, which is impractical in a large, populous country.

questions.stem: Freedom of the press is important in a democracy because it
options: allows citizens to get information and hold leaders accountable
allows the press to spread lies without consequence
questions.explanation: A free press informs citizens and exposes wrongdoing, helping to keep leaders accountable.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, the head of the executive arm of the federal government is the
options: Speaker of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: The President is Head of State and head of the federal executive.

questions.stem: The pillars of democracy are best described as
options: the walls of the National Assembly
the institutions and principles that support and sustain democracy
questions.explanation: Pillars of democracy are the supports, such as the people, institutions and the rule of law, on which democracy stands.

questions.stem: Majority rule and minority rights means that
options: the minority must always be silenced
the majority decides but the views and rights of the minority are respected
questions.explanation: In democracy decisions follow the majority, while minorities keep their rights and can freely express their views.

questions.stem: The most important pillar of democracy, from whom political power comes, is
questions.explanation: In a democracy, sovereignty belongs to the people, who give leaders authority through elections.

questions.stem: An independent judiciary is a pillar of democracy because it
options: protects the constitution and citizens' rights against abuse of power
questions.explanation: Independent courts can check abuses by the other arms and protect rights, which sustains democracy.

questions.stem: Which of these is a pillar of democracy?
questions.explanation: The rule of law is one of the pillars of democracy.

questions.stem: If the electoral process in a country is not transparent, the most likely result is that
options: more people will register to vote
citizens will lose confidence in the government that emerges
questions.explanation: An election that is not transparent produces leaders whose legitimacy is doubted, weakening democracy.

questions.stem: Democratic institutions that serve as pillars of democracy include
options: the legislature, judiciary and electoral body
questions.explanation: Institutions such as the legislature, independent judiciary, electoral body and free press support democracy.

questions.stem: A person who has the legal right to vote in an election is called a
questions.explanation: A voter is a qualified citizen who is registered and entitled to vote.

questions.stem: A person who stands for an elective office is called a
questions.explanation: A candidate is a person who contests an election to be chosen for an office.

questions.stem: An election in which voters choose their representatives directly is a
questions.explanation: In a direct election, voters themselves elect the representative; in an indirect election, chosen delegates elect on their behalf.

questions.stem: A general election is one in which
options: only one vacant seat is filled
elections are held for many offices across the country at the end of a term
voters answer yes or no to a policy
questions.explanation: A general election fills elective offices across the country, usually at the end of the tenure of office.

questions.stem: An election held between the two leading candidates when no candidate meets the requirements to win in the first round is a
questions.explanation: A run-off election is held when no candidate meets the constitutional requirements in the first ballot.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, the minimum age for a person to contest for the office of President is
questions.explanation: Following the "Not Too Young To Run" amendment of 2018, the minimum age for President is 35 years.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, the minimum age for a person to contest for a seat in the House of Representatives is
questions.explanation: The 2018 constitutional amendment reduced the minimum age for the House of Representatives from 30 to 25 years.

questions.stem: One basic qualification for a person to vote in Nigeria is that the person must be
options: a member of a political party
a Nigerian citizen of at least 18 years who is registered
questions.explanation: A voter must be a Nigerian citizen, at least 18 years old and on the register of voters.

questions.stem: Which of these is a responsibility of a voter?
options: Selling his vote to the highest bidder
Voting for candidates based on their ability and programmes
questions.explanation: A responsible voter votes freely and wisely for candidates based on merit, not money or sentiment.

questions.stem: A responsible voter who notices an irregularity at a polling unit should
options: set the ballot box on fire
report it peacefully to election officials or security agents
questions.explanation: Voters should report irregularities through lawful channels and avoid violence.

questions.stem: Elections are important in a democracy mainly because they
options: give citizens a peaceful way to choose and change their leaders
allow leaders to stay in power for life
questions.explanation: Elections allow peaceful transfer of power and make leaders accountable to the people.

questions.stem: The document a person who wants to contest an election uses to tell voters what he or she will do if elected is the
questions.explanation: A manifesto sets out a candidate's or party's programmes and promises.

questions.stem: Voting by a person who is below 18 years of age is called
questions.explanation: Underage voting is a form of electoral malpractice.

questions.stem: Using thugs to frighten voters away from polling units is called
questions.explanation: Thuggery and intimidation are forms of electoral malpractice that deny people free choice.

questions.stem: Deliberately holding back ballot papers and result sheets so that some areas cannot vote is known as
questions.explanation: Creating artificial scarcity of electoral materials is a malpractice aimed at disenfranchising voters.

questions.stem: A politician who makes promises he knows he cannot or will not fulfil in order to win votes is using
questions.explanation: Fake manifestoes deceive voters and are listed among electoral malpractices.

questions.stem: Changing the figures on a result sheet after votes have been counted is known as
questions.explanation: Altering results after counting is manipulation of votes, a serious electoral offence.

questions.stem: Which of these is the MOST likely effect of electoral malpractice on voter turnout in future elections?
options: Everyone will vote more than once
The number of political parties will reduce to zero
Many people may refuse to vote because they believe their votes will not count
questions.explanation: When people believe elections are rigged, they lose interest and turnout falls.

questions.stem: Which of these practices is NOT an electoral malpractice?
options: Peaceful campaigning on a party's programmes
questions.explanation: Peaceful campaigning is a legitimate part of elections; the others are malpractices.

questions.stem: Printing extra ballot papers that were not issued by the electoral body is an example of
questions.explanation: Fake ballot papers are a form of rigging and electoral malpractice.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: INEC stands for
questions.explanation: INEC is the Independent National Electoral Commission.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: SIEC stands for
questions.explanation: Each state has a State Independent Electoral Commission that conducts local government elections.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of these is a function of INEC?
options: Trying election offenders as a court
questions.explanation: INEC registers political parties and conducts federal and state elections; local council elections are conducted by SIECs.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: The card issued by INEC that a registered voter presents to vote is the
questions.explanation: Registered voters receive a Permanent Voter Card, which they use for accreditation.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: Free and fair elections ensure that
options: the candidates chosen by the majority of voters win
questions.explanation: Free and fair elections allow voters' true choices to determine the winners.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: Which of the following would MOST help INEC to conduct credible elections?
options: Independence from political interference and adequate funding
questions.explanation: An independent, well-funded electoral body with trained staff can conduct credible elections.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: Disputes arising from governorship elections in Nigeria are first decided by
questions.explanation: Election petition tribunals hear disputes from elections; appeals may go to higher courts.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: Elections in Nigeria for federal and state offices are conducted by
questions.explanation: INEC conducts elections for President, National Assembly, Governors and State Houses of Assembly.

questions.topic: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
questions.stem: Election observers, both local and international, help to
options: monitor and report on whether an election is credible
questions.explanation: Observers watch the conduct of elections and report on their credibility, which discourages malpractice.

questions.stem: The process of entering the names and details of qualified voters into the voters' register is called
questions.explanation: Voter registration records eligible citizens so they can vote.

questions.stem: The place where voters go to cast their votes is the
questions.explanation: Voters cast their votes at their assigned polling units.

questions.stem: Checking that a voter is registered and verifying the voter's card before voting is called
questions.explanation: Accreditation confirms that the voter is on the register and qualified to vote at that unit.

questions.stem: The ongoing exercise by INEC that allows citizens who have just turned 18 to register is called
questions.explanation: Continuous voter registration lets newly qualified citizens and others register between elections.

questions.stem: After a voter marks the ballot paper in the voting cubicle, the voter should
options: fold it and drop it in the ballot box
questions.explanation: The marked ballot is folded to keep it secret and dropped in the ballot box.

questions.stem: The bringing together of results from many polling units to get the total for a ward or constituency is called
questions.explanation: Collation is the adding up of results from polling units at higher levels.

questions.stem: Why is voting by secret ballot important?
options: It allows party agents to know how everyone voted
It protects voters from intimidation and allows a free choice
It allows people to vote many times
questions.explanation: Secrecy means no one can punish or reward a voter for their choice, so voters choose freely.

questions.stem: Voting is important because it
options: allows citizens to avoid paying tax
makes citizens members of the army
allows citizens to take part in choosing their leaders
questions.explanation: Through voting, citizens participate in government and choose their representatives.

questions.stem: A registered voter who wants to vote must normally vote at
options: the polling unit where he or she registered
questions.explanation: Voters are registered to specific polling units and normally vote there.

questions.topic: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of honesty. [2 marks]
(b) State four consequences of dishonesty in Nigerian society. [4 marks]
(c) Give four benefits of cooperation among members of a community. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Honesty is being truthful, fair and sincere in words and actions; not lying, cheating or stealing
1 mark: (b) Loss of trust between people / between citizens and government
1 mark: (b) Examination malpractice and worthless certificates
1 mark: (b) Corruption, fraud and waste of public funds
1 mark: (b) Punishment such as dismissal, imprisonment or bad name / poor national image
1 mark: (c) Harmony and peace in the community
1 mark: (c) Faster achievement of common goals
1 mark: (c) Progress and development (e.g. roads, markets built through self-help)
1 mark: (c) Sharing of resources and support for the needy
questions.explanation: Honesty means truthfulness and sincerity. Dishonesty destroys trust, encourages malpractice and corruption, and brings punishment and a bad image. Cooperation brings harmony, progress, goal achievement and mutual support. Accept any other valid points.

questions.topic: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
questions.stem:
(a) What is discipline? [2 marks]
(b) List four attributes of a disciplined person. [4 marks]
(c) Explain the three types of courage with an example of each. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Discipline is self-control and behaving according to rules, regulations and accepted standards
1 mark: (b) Self-control
1 mark: (b) Respect for rules and legitimate authority
1 mark: (b) Moderation / modesty
1 mark: (b) Perseverance / dedication
2 marks: (c) Physical courage: facing physical danger or pain, e.g. rescuing someone from a fire
2 marks: (c) Moral courage: standing for what is right despite opposition, e.g. refusing to join in cheating or reporting wrongdoing
2 marks: (c) Spiritual courage: inner strength from faith or conviction, e.g. remaining hopeful and firm during hardship
questions.explanation: Discipline is self-control and obedience to rules. Attributes include self-control, moderation, modesty, respect for authority, perseverance and dedication. The three types of courage are physical, moral and spiritual; award 1 mark for each explanation and 1 for a suitable example.

questions.stem:
(a) What is negative behaviour? [2 marks]
(b) Mention four types of negative behaviour common among Nigerian youths. [4 marks]
(c) Suggest four ways of promoting positive behaviour in schools. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Behaviour that is contrary to accepted values and harmful to the individual or society
1 mark: (b) Examination malpractice
1 mark: (b) Cultism
1 mark: (b) Drug abuse / drug trafficking
1 mark: (b) Dishonesty, disregard for time or ostentatious living
1 mark: (c) Rewarding good behaviour
1 mark: (c) Teachers and parents serving as role models
1 mark: (c) Enforcing school rules fairly
1 mark: (c) Guidance and counselling / values education and clubs
questions.explanation: Negative behaviour goes against accepted values. Examples include exam malpractice, cultism, drug abuse, dishonesty and lateness. Positive behaviour is promoted by rewards, role models, fair rules and counselling. Accept other valid answers.

questions.stem:
(a) Who is a citizen? [2 marks]
(b) Explain the three ways of becoming a citizen of Nigeria. [6 marks]
(c) State two duties of a citizen. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A citizen is a legal member of a country who enjoys full rights and performs duties to it
2 marks: (b) By birth: born to parents or grandparents who are Nigerian citizens
2 marks: (b) By registration: e.g. a foreign woman married to a Nigerian man, or a person born abroad to a Nigerian grandparent, who applies and is registered
2 marks: (b) By naturalisation: a foreigner who has lived in Nigeria for the required period, is of good character and takes the oath of allegiance
1 mark: (c) Obeying the laws / paying taxes
1 mark: (c) Defending the country / voting / respecting national symbols
questions.explanation: Citizenship can be acquired by birth, registration or naturalisation as provided by the constitution. Duties include obeying laws, paying tax, voting and defending the nation.

questions.topic: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
questions.stem:
(a) Differentiate between rights and duties. [4 marks]
(b) List four fundamental human rights in the Nigerian constitution. [4 marks]
(c) Give two reasons why citizens should perform their duties. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Rights are the freedoms and benefits a citizen is entitled to enjoy from the state
2 marks: (a) Duties are the obligations a citizen owes to the state and society
1 mark: (b) Right to life
1 mark: (b) Right to dignity of the human person / personal liberty
1 mark: (b) Right to fair hearing
1 mark: (b) Freedom of expression, movement, religion or association / right to own property
1 mark: (c) To maintain peace, order and social control
1 mark: (c) To help government provide services and develop the nation
questions.explanation: Rights are what citizens enjoy; duties are what citizens owe. Chapter IV rights include life, dignity, liberty, fair hearing, privacy, thought and religion, expression, assembly, movement, freedom from discrimination and property.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a constitution? [2 marks]
(b) State two features each of the Clifford Constitution of 1922 and the Richards Constitution of 1946. [8 marks]
(c) Mention one feature of the 1979 Constitution. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A body of fundamental rules and principles according to which a state is governed
2 marks: (b) Clifford: introduced the elective principle
2 marks: (b) Clifford: elected members for Lagos (3) and Calabar (1) in the Legislative Council
2 marks: (b) Richards: introduced regionalism / divided Nigeria into three regions with regional houses of assembly
2 marks: (b) Richards: brought the North and South together in one central Legislative Council with an unofficial majority
2 marks: (c) Presidential system with an executive president / federal character principle / 19 states
questions.explanation: Clifford (1922) introduced the elective principle; Richards (1946) introduced regionalism and united North and South in one Legislative Council. The 1979 Constitution introduced the presidential system and the Federal Character principle.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four national symbols of Nigeria. [4 marks]
(b) What do the following represent on the Nigerian coat of arms: (i) the eagle (ii) the two horses (iii) the black shield? [3 marks]
(c) State three purposes for which the NYSC was established. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) National flag
1 mark: (a) Coat of arms
1 mark: (a) National anthem
1 mark: (a) National pledge / national currency
1 mark: (b)(i) Strength
1 mark: (b)(ii) Dignity
1 mark: (b)(iii) Fertile soil
1 mark: (c) To promote national unity and integration
1 mark: (c) To expose graduates to cultures of other parts of the country
1 mark: (c) To develop a spirit of service, self-reliance and patriotism among youths
questions.explanation: National symbols include the flag, coat of arms, anthem, pledge and currency. On the coat of arms the eagle stands for strength, the horses for dignity and the black shield for fertile soil. The NYSC promotes unity, cultural exposure and service.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a federation? [2 marks]
(b) State four features of a federal system of government. [4 marks]
(c) Give four reasons why Nigeria adopted federalism. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A system of government in which powers are shared between a central government and component units (states) by the constitution
1 mark: (b) Division of powers between the central and state governments
1 mark: (b) A written and rigid constitution
1 mark: (b) A supreme court to settle disputes between tiers
1 mark: (b) Each tier has constitutionally defined control over its own affairs / bicameral legislature
1 mark: (c) Ethnic, cultural and religious diversity (unity in diversity)
1 mark: (c) Large size of the country
1 mark: (c) To protect minority groups / allay fear of domination
1 mark: (c) To bring government closer to the people / colonial heritage
questions.explanation: Federalism shares power constitutionally between levels of government. Nigeria adopted it because of diversity, size, fear of domination and the colonial background.

questions.topic: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
questions.stem:
(a) Name the three tiers of government in Nigeria. [3 marks]
(b) Distinguish between the Exclusive List and the Concurrent List, giving one example of each. [4 marks]
(c) State three functions of local governments. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Federal government
1 mark: (a) State government
1 mark: (a) Local government
2 marks: (b) Exclusive List: matters on which only the federal government can legislate, e.g. defence, currency, foreign affairs
2 marks: (b) Concurrent List: matters on which both federal and state governments can legislate, e.g. post-primary education, electricity, agricultural development
1 mark: (c) Registration of births, deaths and marriages
1 mark: (c) Provision and maintenance of markets, motor parks and local roads
1 mark: (c) Collection of rates and local taxes / primary health care / refuse disposal
questions.explanation: The three tiers are federal, state and local governments. Exclusive matters are federal only; concurrent matters are shared, with federal law prevailing in a conflict. Local governments run markets, motor parks, local roads and registration of births and deaths.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the term "rule of law". [2 marks]
(b) State three principles of the rule of law. [3 marks]
(c) Give five benefits of the rule of law over arbitrary rule. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A situation in which the law is supreme and everyone, including government, is subject to it
1 mark: (b) Supremacy of the law
1 mark: (b) Equality before the law
1 mark: (b) Respect for fundamental rights / fair hearing
1 mark: (c) Protection of citizens' rights
1 mark: (c) Prevents abuse of power by leaders
1 mark: (c) Promotes peace and order
1 mark: (c) Ensures fair trial for accused persons
1 mark: (c) Encourages investment and development / builds trust in government
questions.explanation: Rule of law means the law is supreme and applies equally to all. Its principles, as explained by A. V. Dicey, are supremacy of law, equality before the law and protection of rights. It protects rights and restrains leaders, unlike arbitrary rule.

questions.stem:
(a) Who is a consumer? [2 marks]
(b) List four rights of a consumer. [4 marks]
(c) State four responsibilities of a consumer. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A person who buys or uses goods and services to satisfy personal needs
1 mark: (b) Right to safety
1 mark: (b) Right to information
1 mark: (b) Right to redress
1 mark: (b) Right to be heard / consumer education / satisfaction of basic needs / healthy environment
1 mark: (c) Be aware of quality, price and expiry dates
1 mark: (c) Demand and keep receipts, invoices and warranties
1 mark: (c) Think independently
1 mark: (c) Speak out / respect the environment
questions.explanation: Consumers have rights to basic needs, safety, information, redress, education, representation and a healthy environment, and responsibilities to be aware, keep proof of purchase, think independently, speak out and respect the environment.

questions.stem:
(a) What are the pillars of democracy? [2 marks]
(b) Explain four pillars of democracy. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The institutions and principles on which democracy stands and which sustain it
2 marks: (b) The people: the source of political power who elect leaders
2 marks: (b) Rule of law: everyone, including leaders, is subject to the law
2 marks: (b) Transparent electoral process: free, fair and credible elections
2 marks: (b) Majority rule and minority rights / democratic institutions such as an independent judiciary, legislature and free press
questions.explanation: Award 2 marks for each pillar correctly explained (1 for naming, 1 for explanation). Accept independent judiciary, free press, political parties and constitutionalism as democratic institutions.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following: (i) election (ii) by-election (iii) referendum. [6 marks]
(b) State four responsibilities of a voter. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Election: the process of choosing representatives or leaders by voting
2 marks: (a)(ii) By-election: an election to fill a seat that becomes vacant before the end of the term
2 marks: (a)(iii) Referendum: a vote in which citizens decide directly on an important issue
1 mark: (b) Register and collect the voter card
1 mark: (b) Vote peacefully and only once
1 mark: (b) Vote for candidates based on merit and not for money
1 mark: (b) Report electoral malpractice / protect the voter card / obey electoral laws
questions.explanation: Elections choose leaders; by-elections fill vacancies; referendums decide issues directly. Voters must register, vote once and wisely, resist inducement and report malpractice.

questions.stem:
(a) What is electoral malpractice? [2 marks]
(b) Mention four forms of electoral malpractice. [4 marks]
(c) Suggest four ways of preventing electoral malpractice in Nigeria. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Any illegal act or practice that undermines the free and fair conduct of an election
1 mark: (b) Multiple voting / fake ballot papers
1 mark: (b) Vote buying (inducement)
1 mark: (b) Thuggery and intimidation / ballot box snatching
1 mark: (b) Underage voting / manipulation of results / artificial scarcity of materials
1 mark: (c) Strengthening the independence of INEC
1 mark: (c) Voter education
1 mark: (c) Prosecuting and punishing electoral offenders
1 mark: (c) Use of technology for accreditation and result transmission / adequate security at polling units
questions.explanation: Electoral malpractice includes all illegal acts that corrupt an election. Prevention involves an independent electoral body, voter education, punishment of offenders, technology and security.
